transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I can’t stop noticing this drooping and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It’s in every photo, every reflection. People tell me I look fine, but it feels really obvious to me, and I’ve started avoiding presentations and meeting with clients because of it.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about how your mouth or jaw looks?

Yes. It’s on my mind all the time. I keep seeing the droop around my mouth and how uneven my jaw looks in photos or mirrors. Even if someone says they don’t notice it, I can’t believe them—it feels very obvious to me.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your mouth or jaw in mirrors or photos?

Yes. Before work or a family event, I can spend hours in the bathroom mirror and taking pictures on my phone from different angles. I redo my makeup, adjust my scarf, and ask my husband over and over if my face looks lopsided. Then I end up looking through other women’s photos and comparing myself to them.
When you avoid presentations or meeting with clients, is it mainly because you’re afraid other people will notice and judge your mouth or jaw?

Yes. I feel like everyone will see it right away and judge me. I cancelled a major client presentation at the last minute because I just couldn’t stand being up there. I’ve also been missing networking events connected to awards, and it’s starting to affect my deadlines and even family gatherings.
If you didn’t have this concern about your mouth and jaw, would you still be afraid of presentations or meeting with clients?

No, I don’t think so. If I didn’t feel so upset about being seen, I’d be able to do the presentations and meet clients. I’ve already cancelled a major presentation and skipped networking for awards, and now my deadlines and even family gatherings are starting to fall apart because of it.
Has a doctor or dentist ever told you there is actually something wrong with your mouth or jaw?

No. No doctor or dentist has told me there’s a problem. But I see this drooping and unevenness around my mouth and jaw every time I look in a mirror or photo. People say I look fine, but it feels obvious to me.
Do you do these checking behaviors mainly because of your concern about how your mouth and jaw look?

Yes. Before work or a family event, I can spend hours in the bathroom mirror, taking pictures from different angles, redoing my makeup or adjusting my scarf. I keep asking my husband if my face looks lopsided. Then I’ll look through photos of other women and compare myself to them. It’s all because of how my mouth and jaw look.
Are these repeated checking behaviors mainly because you feel there is something wrong with how your face looks?

Yes. It’s because I feel my face looks wrong—especially lopsided around my mouth and jaw. Before work or family events, I can lose hours checking the mirror, taking pictures from different angles, fixing my makeup and scarf, and asking my husband how it looks. Then I compare my photos with other women’s pictures.
Are the thoughts you can’t stop having mainly about your mouth and jaw looking uneven?

Yes. It’s mostly the drooping and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. I see it in every reflection or photo, and I can’t get it out of my mind, even when people tell me I look fine. It’s gotten bad enough that I avoid presentations and seeing clients.
Are the upsetting thoughts you can’t control mainly about a flaw in your appearance?

Yes. I can’t stop focusing on the droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It shows up to me in every mirror or photo, and even if people say I look fine, it still feels really obvious. It’s made me avoid presentations and meeting with clients.
Do you believe for certain that your mouth and jaw are actually deformed?
I mean, it feels certain when I see myself. The droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw look so obvious in photos and reflections, even though other people tell me I look fine.
Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about how noticeable the drooping and unevenness are?

I guess it’s possible, since people keep telling me I look fine. But when I see a photo or my reflection, the droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw just look so obvious to me. I can’t stop noticing it.
Aside from worries about how your mouth and jaw look, do you also get other unwanted thoughts that lead you to do repetitive rituals or checking?

It’s mostly about my appearance. Before work or a family event, I can spend hours in the bathroom mirror, taking pictures from different angles, redoing my makeup or scarf. I keep asking my husband whether my face looks lopsided, then I end up looking through photos of other women and comparing myself to them.
Are you mainly preoccupied with a flaw in your appearance?

Yes. I can’t stop focusing on the droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It’s in every photo or reflection to me, even when people say I look fine. It feels so obvious that I’ve started avoiding presentations and meeting with clients.
Are you completely certain that your mouth and jaw really look abnormal?

I mean, I know people tell me I look fine, so maybe I could be wrong. But when I see myself in photos or the mirror, the droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw look completely obvious to me. It’s hard for me to see it any other way.
In social situations where your face is not the focus, do you still feel afraid that people will judge you?

Yes. I’ve cancelled a major client presentation at the last minute, and I’ve been skipping networking events connected to awards because I just can’t face being seen. It’s starting to affect my project deadlines, and even family gatherings are falling apart around it.
If you were not worried about how your mouth and jaw look, would you still be afraid people would judge you in social situations?

No, I don’t think so. It’s really the way my mouth and jaw look that makes me feel like people will notice and judge me. If I didn’t see that droop and unevenness, I don’t think I’d be avoiding presentations or clients like this.
